quiz.title: Unit 2 skill drill: Revise an overly broad claim into an arguable claim with a line of reasoning.
quiz.headline: Revise an overly broad claim into an arguable claim with a line of reasoning.
quiz.prompt: A student writes: “Trade changed everything.” Rewrite it as a defensible Unit 2 thesis.
quiz.instructions: Write a short response, then open the worked example and compare. This checklist is practice and does not produce an official AP score.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice. Rubric categories follow the structure of the College Board's AP history rubrics; scoring here is your own self-assessment, not an official score.

responseFields.label: Your response
responseFields.prompt: Write your revised thesis and one sentence explaining why it is stronger.

rubric.label: Skill checklist
rubric.guidance: The thesis is limited to a time and place, makes a claim someone could dispute, and previews a line of reasoning.

quiz.modelResponse:
Worked example: “Between 1200 and 1450, expanding trade strengthened states that could tax it, such as Mali and Malacca, and spread Islam to new regions, but these changes were uneven because many rural communities kept older economies and beliefs.”

Why it is stronger: it sets a time period, names specific states, makes a claim a reader could argue against, previews two lines of reasoning (state power and religion), and qualifies the claim instead of saying trade changed “everything.”
quiz.alternateModel: Another strong thesis could focus on environmental effects: “Trade networks spread both useful crops and deadly disease, so connectivity raised food supplies in some regions while the plague cut populations sharply in others.”
commonErrors: Restating the prompt without making a claim.
Naming topics without explaining how they connect to the claim.
Making a claim so broad that no evidence could disprove it.

scaffold.label: Narrow
scaffold.text: Set a time, place, or group.

scaffold.label: Claim
scaffold.text: Say what changed and how much.

scaffold.label: Reason
scaffold.text: Preview why, with two categories of evidence.

checklist: Limits the claim to a time period and specific places.
Makes a claim that a reader could argue against.
Previews at least two reasons or categories of evidence.
